scenes.heading: Building a signature style without becoming repetitive

sents.d: Building a signature style without becoming repetitive
A recognizable style helps marketing, but rigid repetition limits client fit.

scenes.heading: A point of view is an asset

sents.d: A consistent point of view — recurring color sensibilities, typography choices, or compositional habits — makes your portfolio feel cohesive and helps potential clients quickly understand what to expect from working with you.
The risk is applying the same solution regardless of the client's actual brand and audience, which can result in client work that all looks the same regardless of who it was made for.

scenes.heading: Serve the client, not the habit

sents.d: A useful check is asking whether a design decision was made because it genuinely served that specific client's brand and audience, or simply because it's a habit you default to — the former builds a style, the latter risks becoming a limitation.

take: Keep a style, but make every decision for the client.
